newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 25.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 25:

TEL AVIV - The historic experiment in Israeli-Palestinian peace, briefly buoyed by January's Hebron deal, now appears to be in the worst trouble since the two sides reached mutual recognition in September 1993.
WASHINGTON - Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is elevating the importance of women's issues on America's international agenda, stressing rights gains as a central foreign policy objective.
WASHINGTON - For two centuries, not much has changed in western Montgomery County, the land that suburban sprawl forgot.

WASHINGTON - Mary Treadwell, an employee of the D.C. mayor's office who served 15 months in federal prison on a 1983 fraud conviction, "improperly diverted" and has not accounted for more than $10,000 allocated by the District for community services, according to a D.C. auditor's report.

WASHINGTON - Over the past 30 years, about four million Americans have contracted hepatitis C, an infection of the liver that usually is life-long and incurable. What will happen to those people is one of contemporary medicine's biggest and unanswered questions.
WASHINGTON - On May 1, Maryland will become the first state in the nation in which 10-digit dialling is required for all local telephone calls.
